leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Comparative Adjectives
leadIn.content: Comparing two items: A train is faster than a bus, and a city is more expensive than a village.

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Comparative Adjectives?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Comparative Adjectives require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Comparative Adjectives
form.content: Short adjectives: adj + -er + than (faster than). Long adjectives: more + adj + than (more expensive than). Irregular: good -> better, bad -> worse.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Comparative Adjectives
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Comparative Adjectives.

controlledPractice.question: Comparative of 'big'?
controlledPractice.explanation: Consonant+vowel+consonant → double the final letter: big → bigger.

controlledPractice.question: Comparative of 'expensive'?
controlledPractice.explanation: Long adjectives (2+ syllables) use 'more' instead of changing the word.

controlledPractice.question: Comparative of 'good'?
controlledPractice.explanation: Good → better is an irregular special form.
